When you look up during the day, your eye detects this scattered blue light coming from all directions of the sky, rather than the direct path of the sun. This makes the sky appear blue. At sunrise or sunset, sunlight passes through more atmosphere, scattering away most blue light before it reaches your eyes, leaving the longer wavelengths (reds and oranges) visible.

def longest_palindrome(s: str) -> str:
    if not s:
        return ""
    
    start, end = 0, 0
    
    def expand_around_center(left: int, right: int) -> int:
        """Expands outward from the given center while characters match."""
        while left >= 0 and right < len(s) and s[left] == s[right]:
            left -= 1
            right += 1
        # Return the length of the palindrome found (right - left - 1)
        return right - left - 1

    for i in range(len(s)):
        # Check for odd-length palindromes (single center)
        len1 = expand_around_center(i, i)
        # Check for even-length palindromes (two center characters)
        len2 = expand_around_center(i, i + 1)
        # Update the longest palindrome found so far
        max_len = max(len1, len2)
        if max_len > end - start:
            start = i - (max_len - 1) // 2
            end = i + max_len // 2

    return s[start:end + 1]
